# Tackle Design System

React components and design tokens built from the Tackle Design Library (Figma).

## Setup

Add the following to your `~/.npmrc` to access the package from GitHub Packages:

```
@tackle-io:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com/
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=YOUR_GITHUB_PAT
```

Create a token at https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=read:packages with the `read:packages` scope.

## Create a Prototype

Scaffold a new app with the design system pre-configured:

```bash
npx @tackle-io/design-system@alpha create prototype --name my-prototype
cd my-prototype
npm run dev
```

| Option            | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--name <name>`   | Project directory name (required)                                                                                                    |
| `--shell <shell>` | Application shell: `platform`, `salesforce-opportunity`, or `salesforce-drilldown`. Unknown or omitted values default to `platform`. |

Each shell scaffolds a runnable Vite + React + TypeScript app that matches the corresponding Storybook story:

| Shell                    | Component                    | What you get                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `platform`               | `ApplicationShell`           | Tackle Platform sidebar (default nav items, Co-Sell active) with a placeholder `HomePage`.                      |
| `salesforce-opportunity` | `SalesforceOpportunityShell` | Salesforce Lightning–style Opportunity record page with highlights, sales path, tabs, and `TackleCard` sidebar. |
| `salesforce-drilldown`   | `SalesforceDrilldownShell`   | Salesforce Lightning–style drill-down form page with breadcrumb, quick-links sidebar, and sticky action bar.    |

### Cursor Skill (optional)

Install the skill to let Cursor scaffold prototypes for you:

```bash
npx skills@latest add tackle-io/design-system/skills/create-tackle-prototype -g -a cursor
```

| Flag / Argument     | Description                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npx skills@latest` | Runs the latest version of the `skills` CLI without installing it globally                  |
| `add <path>`        | Installs a skill from the given GitHub repo path into your local skill registry             |
| `-g`                | Installs the skill globally (available across all projects, not just the current workspace) |
| `-a cursor`         | Targets the **Cursor** agent — tells the CLI which AI agent the skill is for                |

Then ask your agent: _"create a Tackle prototype"_

## Add to an Existing Project

```bash
npm install @tackle-io/design-system
# or
pnpm add @tackle-io/design-system
```

```tsx
import '@tackle-io/design-system/styles';
import { Button } from '@tackle-io/design-system';
```

See [QUICK_START.md](./QUICK_START.md) for framework integration guides (CSS variables, Tailwind, MUI, TypeScript).

## 🎨 What's Included

This package provides design tokens in multiple formats:

- **JSON tokens** - Framework-agnostic token definitions
- **CSS Custom Properties** - Standard CSS variables
- **Tailwind Configuration** - Ready-to-use Tailwind theme
- **MUI Theme** - Material-UI theme configuration
- **TypeScript Types** - Full type safety for tokens

## 🚀 Usage

### CSS Custom Properties

Import the CSS variables file in your application:

```css
@import '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens/variables.css';

/* Use tokens in your CSS */
.button {
  background-color: var(--color-primary);
  padding: var(--spacing-md);
  border-radius: var(--border-radius-base);
  box-shadow: var(--elevation-200);
}
```

### Tailwind CSS

Extend your Tailwind configuration:

```js
// tailwind.config.js
const tackleTokens = require('@tackle-io/design-system/tailwind.config.js');

module.exports = {
  ...tackleTokens,
  content: [
    './src/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}'
    // your content paths
  ],
  // You can override or extend further if needed
  theme: {
    ...tackleTokens.theme,
    extend: {
      ...tackleTokens.theme.extend
      // Your custom extensions
    }
  }
};
```

Use in your React components:

```tsx
function Button() {
  return (
    <button className="bg-primary text-neutral-0 px-md py-sm rounded-base shadow-200 hover:shadow-300">
      Click me
    </button>
  );
}
```

### Material-UI (MUI)

Wrap your app with the Tackle theme:

```tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from '@mui/material/styles';
import tackleTheme from '@tackle-io/design-system/mui-theme';

function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider theme={tackleTheme}>
      {/* Your app components */}
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

### TypeScript / JavaScript

Import tokens directly in your code:

```tsx
import {
  theme,
  colorValues,
  spacingValues
} from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens';

// Use typed tokens
const Button = styled.button`
  background-color: ${theme.colors.primary};
  padding: ${theme.spacing.md};
  border-radius: ${theme.borderRadius.base};
  box-shadow: ${theme.elevation[200]};
`;

// Or use individual token categories
const primaryColor = colorValues.primary;
const mediumSpacing = spacingValues.md;
```

### Raw JSON Tokens

Access raw token definitions:

```ts
import colors from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens/colors.json';
import spacing from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens/spacing.json';
import typography from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens/typography.json';
import elevation from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens/elevation.json';

// Token structure: { value: string, type: string }
const primaryBlue = colors.color.blue[40].value; // "#2684FF"
```

## 📖 Token Reference

### Colors

```ts
// Color scales (10-90)
colorValues.red[50]; // #FF5630
colorValues.yellow[40]; // #FFC400
colorValues.green[50]; // #36B37E
colorValues.blue[40]; // #2684FF
colorValues.purple[50]; // #6554C0
colorValues.neutral[100]; // #091E42

// Semantic colors
colorValues.primary; // #2684FF
colorValues.success; // #36B37E
colorValues.warning; // #FFC400
colorValues.error; // #FF5630
colorValues.info; // #2684FF
```

### Spacing

```ts
spacingValues.xs; // 8px
spacingValues.sm; // 16px
spacingValues.md; // 24px
spacingValues.lg; // 40px
spacingValues.xl; // 64px
```

### Typography

```ts
// Font sizes
typographyValues.fontSize.hero; // 40px
typographyValues.fontSize.h1; // 36px
typographyValues.fontSize.body; // 16px
typographyValues.fontSize.small; // 12px

// Font weights
typographyValues.fontWeight.light; // 300
typographyValues.fontWeight.regular; // 400
typographyValues.fontWeight.semibold; // 600
typographyValues.fontWeight.bold; // 700

// Font families
typographyValues.fontFamily.primary; // 'Open Sans', sans-serif
typographyValues.fontFamily.code; // 'Inconsolata', monospace
```

### Elevation (Shadows)

```ts
elevationValues[100]; // Minimal elevation
elevationValues[200]; // Cards, tiles
elevationValues[300]; // Raised cards
elevationValues[400]; // Modals, popovers
elevationValues['500L']; // Left directional shadow
elevationValues['500R']; // Right directional shadow
```

### Layout

```ts
// Breakpoints
theme.breakpoints.mobile; // 768px
theme.breakpoints.tablet; // 1024px
theme.breakpoints.desktop; // 1440px

// Icon sizes
theme.iconSize.small; // 16px
theme.iconSize.medium; // 24px
theme.iconSize.large; // 32px
theme.iconSize.xl; // 64px
```

## 🎯 Best Practices

### Component Development

1. **Use semantic color names** for better maintainability:

   ```tsx
   // ✅ Good
   <Button color="primary" />

   // ❌ Avoid
   <Button color="blue-40" />
   ```

2. **Use spacing tokens consistently**:

   ```tsx
   // ✅ Good
   <div className="p-md gap-sm" />

   // ❌ Avoid
   <div className="p-6" />
   ```

3. **Match elevation to component hierarchy**:
   - Cards: `elevation-200`
   - Raised cards: `elevation-300`
   - Modals: `elevation-400`

### Accessibility

- All color combinations meet WCAG AA contrast ratios (4.5:1 for normal text)
- Use semantic colors for consistent meaning across the app
- Text colors are predefined with proper contrast

### Responsive Design

```tsx
// Use breakpoint tokens for consistency
const Container = styled.div`
  @media (min-width: ${theme.breakpoints.tablet}) {
    padding: ${theme.spacing.lg};
  }
`;
```

## 🔧 Framework Integration Examples

### Styled Components

```tsx
import styled from 'styled-components';
import { theme } from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens';

const Card = styled.div`
  background: ${theme.colors.neutral[0]};
  padding: ${theme.spacing.md};
  border-radius: ${theme.borderRadius.base};
  box-shadow: ${theme.elevation[200]};
`;
```

### Emotion

```tsx
import { css } from '@emotion/react';
import { theme } from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens';

const buttonStyles = css`
  background-color: ${theme.colors.primary};
  padding: ${theme.spacing.sm} ${theme.spacing.md};
  border-radius: ${theme.borderRadius.base};
`;
```

### Vanilla CSS Modules

```css
/* styles.module.css */
.button {
  background-color: var(--color-primary);
  padding: var(--spacing-sm) var(--spacing-md);
  border-radius: var(--border-radius-base);
}
```

## 📝 Token Structure

Tokens follow a consistent structure:

```json
{
  "value": "string",
  "type": "color | spacing | fontSize | fontWeight | boxShadow | etc."
}
```

This structure is compatible with tools like:

- Style Dictionary
- Figma Tokens
- Design Token specification (W3C Community Group)

## 🔄 Updating Tokens

Tokens are synchronized with the Tackle Design Library Figma file. When updates are needed:

1. Update tokens in Figma
2. Export updated token values
3. Run token generation script (if automated)
4. Review changes and update version

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for full contributor docs (agent skills setup, smoke-test loop, component additions, migration from `.cursor/skills/`).

### Local Development

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tackle-io/design-system.git
cd design-system
npm run setup        # npm install + install agent skills into .agents/skills/
npm run dev          # Start dev server
npm run storybook    # Component documentation
npm test             # Run tests
npm run build        # Build the library
```

`npm run setup` runs `npm install` and copies the skills under `/skills/` and `/skills-internal/` into `.agents/skills/`, where Cursor and Claude Code natively discover them. If you have a clone from before the `/skills/` migration, also run `rm -rf .cursor/skills .cursor/rules` to clear the legacy locations (they are now gitignored).

### Manual Installation (Without the Skills CLI)

If `npm run skills:install` cannot reach the `vercel-labs/skills` CLI (offline, network blocked, CLI moved or yanked), copy the source skills into `.agents/skills/` by hand:

```bash
mkdir -p .agents/skills
cp -R skills/. .agents/skills/
cp -R skills-internal/. .agents/skills/
```

Cursor and Claude Code will pick them up on the next conversation. This is functionally equivalent to what `npx skills add` does — the CLI is a convenience, not a hard dependency.

### Testing the CLI Locally

Build, pack, and test the prototype scaffolder against a local tarball:

```bash
npm run build && npm pack
npx --package ./tackle-io-design-system-<version>.tgz design-system create prototype --name test-app --local ./tackle-io-design-system-<version>.tgz
```

The `--local` flag tells the CLI to use the provided `.tgz` file as the design system dependency instead of resolving from the registry.

### Publishing

> **Note:** This is a manual process used during early alpha development. A proper CI/CD pipeline with automated versioning, changelog generation, and release gating will replace this workflow.

Ensure your `~/.npmrc` has a token with `write:packages` scope, then:

```bash
# 1. Bump the prerelease version (e.g. 0.0.1-alpha.3 → 0.0.1-alpha.4)
npm version prerelease --preid=alpha

# 2. Build the library (runs vite build + tsc via prepublishOnly)
#    and publish to GitHub Packages under the "alpha" dist-tag
#    so it won't become the default "latest" version
npm publish --tag alpha
```
